calls.head: Ottawa’s power play has a target
calls.body: Ottawa ranks 9th of 32 on the power play (7.8 expected goals per 60); Boston ranks 27th on the penalty kill.
calls.call: Ottawa’s power play creates at least its usual 7.8 expected goals per 60.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 1 and 3 games this season
calls.happened: Ottawa had only 0:15 of power-play time, too little to judge.

calls.head: Two of the league’s heaviest-hitting teams
calls.body: Ottawa’s hit score is 114 (3rd of 32) and Boston’s is 106 (10th). 100 is league average, after adjusting for each arena’s scorer.
calls.call: The two teams’ combined hit score reaches their usual 110.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 1 and 3 games this season
calls.happened: The game was rarely close, and hit rates are only counted in close games, so this one can’t be judged.

BOS.head: We gave Boston only a 35% chance, and it went the way we feared.

OTT.head: We gave Ottawa a 65% chance, and Ottawa delivered.

surprises.head: Ottawa shut down Boston’s power play
surprises.body: Boston’s power play created 2.8 expected goals per 60, against its usual 7.8 and a league average of 7.5. Over the last three seasons, a team strayed this far about once every 20 games.

surprises.head: Ottawa was kept to the outside
surprises.body: Ottawa needed 18.8 unblocked shots per expected goal at 5-on-5, against its usual 14.3 and a league average of 15.8. Over the last three seasons, a team strayed this far about once every 10 games.
